class: Any test that asserts elapsed wall-clock time against a fixed threshold (time.perf_counter() - start < N) measures the machine's load, not the code's cost; it fails whenever other work shares the CPU (parallel agents, CI neighbours) and passes on re-run, so a red run carries no information and trains readers to ignore reds.
mechanism: tests/strategy/test_versions.py::test_one_thousand_history_appends_stay_fast asserts 1,001 appends finish in under 1.0 s; with three verifiers and a builder running full suites in parallel it exceeded 1.0 s and passed alone.

first_seen.evidence: verifier: 'Full suite 1217 passed, 1 failed (tests/strategy/test_versions.py::test_one_thousand_history_appends_stay_fast, a timing test); it passed on re-run (30 passed)'

fix: Replace each wall-clock threshold with a deterministic cost check: count the work done (validation calls, comparisons, items re-checked) through an instrumented counter and assert it grows linearly (e.g. 1,000 appends re-validate each event once, not the whole history each time). Keep wall-clock only as a very loose sanity bound, or drop it.
